text:
alex: Noticing a P99 latency jump on prod around 02:10 UTC after last night's infra push. p50 steady, but p99 doubled for short-seq requests. Anyone else seeing this?
priya: Yep, saw the alert. Correlates with the driver bump to NVIDIA 535.86 yesterday evening. Metrics show an uptick in kernel fallbacks during small-seq workloads.
jesse: Quick dump from one affected host: `nvtx` spans show attention kernels falling back to cuBLAS GEMM for seq<=64 in many calls. That smells like kernel selector heuristic misclassification.
morgan: Repro script I used locally (fast):
```
# repro
RD_ENV=staging RUNTIME_KERNEL_LOG=1 ./rd-infer --model rwinf-small --batch-size 8 --seq-len 48 --warmup 20 --iters 200
```
See repeated lines: `selected_kernel: gemm_fallback (score -0.12) vs fused_attn (score 0.07) -> chose gemm_fallback`
alex: Interesting — selector picking gemm despite positive fused_attn score? Maybe there's an alignment/stride check failing downstream. Could be a small bug introduced in the selector refactor.
priya: Also seeing a pattern of KV cache evictions around the same time: the eviction thread spikes and we get a lot of mixed-length batches (some requests with cached prefixes, some without). That changes workspace requirements and might push selector into the safer fallback.
jesse: From the nsys trace (snip):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                      Calls  Avg(ms)
0.34      fused_attention_forward     120    0.0021
1.15      gemm_fallback               480    0.0059
```
But the kernel chooser log shows `expected_workspace=0.8MB, available=0.78MB -> reject fused_attn` for many calls. It's just borderline. The driver update may have changed how free mem is reported (or concurrency with KV evict thread is higher).
morgan: Seen a noisy neighbor effect too — a colocated inference job spiked memory transiently and coincided with selector choosing the fallback. Not purely deterministic.
alex: Can we try two quick mitigations: 1) force selector to prefer fused kernels for seq<=64 (config flag), 2) restart the KV eviction agent to reduce thrash and see if p99 stabilizes?
priya: I'll flip the config on a small shard and push a canary: `runtime.config.kernel_preference.small_seq = fused_attn` and monitor. If that helps, we can do a global rollout.
jesse: For reproability, here's a tight loop that reproduces the p99 on our staging cluster: `wrk -c 16 -t 4 -d 120 --latency http://staging-rd/complete?model=rwinf-small&seq=48` — you'll see 95/99 jump in <2 minutes.
infra-bot: Deploy event: infra/driver-upgrade -> NVIDIA 535.86 applied to fleet at 2026-03-17T23:40:12Z. Contact: @infra oncall.
morgan: Canary result: after pinning kernel_preference on the shard (10 nodes), p99 dropped ~35% within 5 minutes. No other changes.
alex: Good signal. Priya, can you capture a kernel-selector log + nvprof trace from a node before/after restart of kv-evict? Need exact diff to understand whether mem reporting changed or eviction concurrency increased.
priya: On it. Attaching short excerpt when done, but early look shows `cudaMemGetInfo` free bytes fluctuating +-5% more after driver update under same load. That could flip the workspace check for tiny kernels.
jesse: Short-term mitigation: set `RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` in the runtime env for affected pools. Long-term: we need selector to consider eviction-thread reservations and to be tolerant to small mem reporting variance (add hysteresis).
alex: Agree. Opened an issue: ENGRT-1429 "kernel selector borderline rejects fused_attention under small mem variance + KV eviction thrash" and assigned to eng-ml/pri.
morgan: Also raising to eng-sre — maybe we should isolate noisy tenants on dedicated pools while we patch.
priya: Will prepare a PR that introduces a 8% headroom when evaluating workspace (configurable), and a small patch to prefer fused kernels for seq<=64 if score delta < 0.2.
jesse: After applying legacy selector on canary, p99 returned near-baseline. We'll coordinate rollback plan if config flip has side effects.
alex: Thanks team. Next steps: priya PR + canary rollout, eng-sre isolation plan, and monitor for driver reverts from infra. Post updates here. :thumbsup:
morgan: I'll post the nsys full traces and nvprof diffs in the ticket.
infra-bot: Note: planning window open for driver rollback 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC if needed.
